title: Interactive deployment sprint agenda and facilitation notes
body:
Overview:
This is a facilitation-first agenda for a 2-day interactive deployment sprint with a strategic customer. The goal: produce a validated, runnable POC environment (hosted or private) and a prioritized list of next-step work items the customer's infra team can hand to their platform engineers. This doc mixes high-level agenda, slide/slide-deck outline, facilitation prompts, and practical checkpoints (env prep, demo scripts, acceptance tests). Use this as the working source during pre-call planning and live facilitation notes.

Why this format:
- Customers often prefer hands-on outcomes rather than long presentations.
- Split sessions into discovery, configuration, run, and validation to maximize learning and confidence.
- Emphasize measurable acceptance criteria and transfer-of-ownership at the end.

Pre-work (must complete 7 days before sprint):
- Customer to provide a small sample dataset (100–1k rows/texts) and example prompts.
- Access and credentials: either temporary host API key (hosted) or basic VPC connectivity details + k8s creds (private).
- Identify 2 customer liaisons (infra + product) and calendar all required attendees.
- SE to validate demo repo runs locally and share a short checklist: OS, python version, GPU/CPU expectations.
- Run a short smoke test: sample request runs end-to-end within 30s.

Day 0 (asynchronous prep within 48–72 hrs):
- SE task list: provision a customer-scoped workspace (if hosted), or stage configuration manifests (if private).
- Share a 1-page handshake doc: scope, success criteria, rollback plan.

Day 1 morning — Kickoff & discovery (90m):
- Slide 1: Welcome, objectives, and agenda (5m)
- Slide 2: Quick intro of team roles and contact points (5m)
- Facilitator prompt: "What would success look like in 48 hours?" capture verbatim answers. (10m)
- Discovery checklist: primary workload patterns, latency SLOs, expected concurrency, data residency constraints, security controls (KMS/HSM), integration points (webhooks, event systems). Capture as bullets. (30m)
- Alignment: produce a short, agreed success criteria list (3–4 items). Turn these into acceptance tests used on Day 2. (20m)
- Admin: clarify environment (hosted/dedicated/private) and identify missing pre-reqs. (20m)

Day 1 mid — Architecture & rapid design (60m):
- Slide 3: Proposed minimal architecture diagram (1 slide)
- Slide 4: Modes of degradation & fallback policy (1 slide)
- Workshop activity (breakout): two groups (infra & dev/product). Each sketches the integration flow and calls out risk points. Reconvene and consolidate. Output: a single annotated diagram. (30m)
- Decision points log: model family (open vs. proprietary), quantization tradeoffs, routing policies (latency vs cost), caching windows. Tag items as MUST/SHOULD/CAN. (30m)

Day 1 afternoon — Hands-on config & baseline demo (3–4h):
- Task A: Provision tenant/workspace or deploy operator + manifests to a staging cluster. SE leads; customer infra executes.
- Task B: Configure a baseline model (small/quantized) and route a test prompt. Capture token/time/cost numbers.
- Demo script: 1) simple prompt -> 2) streaming run -> 3) KV-cache warmup -> 4) reranker example.
- Data point capture table (SE to fill live): prompt, model, seq_len, latency_p50, latency_p95, token_cost_estimate.
- Facilitator note: watch for env/network errors; have a rollback snapshot or redeploy script handy.

End of Day 1 — Retrospective & plan for Day 2 (30m):
- Quick checklist: Were pre-reqs satisfied? Was baseline demo successful? Blockers and owners logged.
- Set Day 2 goals and assign pre-read (e.g., tuning options, quality monitoring examples).

Day 2 morning — Workload tuning & scale tests (3h):
- Slide 5: Tuning checklist (batching, cache TTLs, quantization profile, sequence length optimization).
- Activity: run 3 workload profiles (low-latency, throughput-heavy, cost-sensitive). For each profile record: throughput, latency histogram, failure rate, per-token cost.
- Facilitation prompt: "If throughput drops by 40% at 2x load, what is acceptable?" Capture target SLO adjustments.

Day 2 mid — Observability & failure modes (90m):
- Slide 6: Console / logging walkthrough (what to look for).
- Run a simulated failure: model OOM or node loss; demonstrate fallback to smaller model or burst to alternate region.
- Build a simple alerting rule during the session and test it (email/Slack).

Day 2 afternoon — Acceptance tests, handoff, and follow-up (2h):
- Execute the acceptance tests defined on Day 1 against the environment. Mark pass/fail and record remediation steps.
- Slide 7: Handoff checklist (credentials, runbook links, ownership matrix).
- Slide 8: Prioritized backlog: list next 8–12 tasks split by "customer", "redwood", "joint" with estimated effort.
- Slide 9: Risk register and recommended mitigations.
- Final facilitation: get explicit sign-off on the agreed acceptance items and next-step owners. Capture signatures (names in doc).

Slide / deck outline (minimal, to be expanded into a 12–15 slide deck):
- Title & goals (1)
- Team & roles (1)
- Initial success criteria (1)
- Minimal architecture & tradeoffs (1)
- Demo plan & baseline metrics (2)
- Tuning & scaling approaches (2)
- Observability & failure recovery (2)
- Handoff & backlog (2)
- Appendices: scripts, sample manifests, acceptance tests (2)

Facilitation scripts & prompts (copyable snippets):
- "Walk me through the user journey where inference matters the most. What happens if latency spikes for 3 minutes?"
- "If we needed to reduce cost by 30% while keeping p95 latency within X ms, which levers would you be comfortable changing?"
- Breakout timeout message: "You have 20 minutes to sketch the integration and three risks — nominate an owner for each."

Common gotchas and mitigations (notes for SEs):
- Missing NACL/Firewall rules: predefined troubleshooting command snippets in appendix.
- Under-powered staging infra: have a plan to run the demo with a lightweight local proxy (lower fidelity but shows flow).
- Sensitive data policies: always use redacted or synthetic datasets; do not store customer PII in shared workspaces.
- Model mismatch: if the selected model underperforms on customer prompts, pivot to a smaller unquantized model for quality checks.

Recording outcomes and artifacts to deliver after sprint:
- A short outcomes doc summarizing acceptance test results and backlog (1–2 pages).
- Config snapshots: manifests, env vars, initial model version pins.
- Runbook draft and a 30-day follow-up plan (owner assignments).
- Optional appendix: raw logs and perf tables exported as CSV.

Quick templates (to copy into the meeting doc):
- Acceptance test line: "Given <input>, when we call <route>, then response meets <latency|accuracy|cost>"
- Backlog item line: "<short title> — owner: <name> — est effort: <points/hours> — type: customer/redwood/joint"

Notes for internal SE prep (private channel):
- Bring a prebuilt quick-fallback manifest for the customer cloud region.
- Pre-seed a small credit-based hosted workspace in case private network prep fails.
- Prepare a canned demo prompt set that highlights hallucination vs factual responses for model evaluation.

Open questions to resolve during pre-call planning:
- Which telemetry retention window does the customer require? (7/30/90 days)
- Are there regulatory controls that force on-premise-only deployments?
- Who will perform long-term quality monitoring on prompts? Customer or Redwood?

Appendix: quick checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Customer sample data received
- [ ] Access/keys provided
- [ ] Stage cluster reachable or hosted workspace provisioned
- [ ] Demo scripts smoke-tested locally
- [ ] Acceptance criteria agreed by both parties

Facilitator final note:
Aim for tangible outcomes: a runnable environment, a set of acceptance tests, and a prioritized handoff plan. Keep sessions interactive and timeboxed. If the customer wants to extend beyond the 2-day scope, capture a formal change request and transition to a Discovery/Scope doc.
